text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 8 in history.
1469 - Florentine painter Fra Filippo Lippi died. He was one of the most important early renaissance painters and a teacher of Botticelli.
1806 - British forces laying siege to the French port of Boulogne used Congreve rockets, invented by Sir William Congreve, the first British use of rocket-propelled missiles.
1810 - James William Marshall, American pioneer, born. His discovery of gold on Sutter's Creek, California, started the gold rush of 1849.
1836 - John Hay, U.S. statesman and diplomat, born. As secretary of state (1898-1905) he promoted the "open door" policy with China.
1856 - Chinese police boarded the British vessel "Arrow", arrested 12 Chinese crewmen on suspicion of piracy and lowered the British flag. The incident led to the second Anglo-Chinese War.
1869 - Franklin Pierce, U.S. politician and 14th president from 1853 to 1857, died.
1871 - The Great Fire of Chicago broke out. According to legend, a cow kicked over a lantern in Mrs O'Leary's barn; 250 people were killed.

1895 - Juan (Domingo) Peron, Argentine general and politician, born. President from 1946 until 1955 when he was deposed in a coup, he was recalled from exile in 1973 and re-elected president. He died in 1974.
1912 - Montenegro declared war on Turkey, beginning the First Balkan War.
1915 - The Battle of Loos ended. It was one of the fiercest battles of World War One with over 420,000 killed, but the British and French gained little ground from the Germans.
1941 - Jesse Jackson, American civil rights leader, born. Regarded as the most powerful black American politician since Martin Luther King Jr.
1952 - 112 people were killed and over 200 injured in a rail crash involving three trains at Harrow and Wealdstone station in north-west London.
1953 - Kathleen Ferrier, world famous British contralto singer, died from cancer at the peak of her career, aged 41.
1953 - Britain and the United States announced they were withdrawing their troops from the Free Territory of Trieste, handing control to the Italians.
1967 - Clement Attlee, British politician and Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951, died. During his six years in office Britain granted independence to India (1947) and Burma (1948).
1970 - The Nobel Prize for Literature went to Russian novelist Alexander Solzhenitsyn.
1982 - The Polish parliament dissolved Solidarity, formally ending eastern Europe's first experiment in trade union democracy.
1990 - United Germany signed its first international treaty, agreeing with Czechoslovakia on a programme for cleaning up the polluted River Elbe.
1990 - Israeli police shot dead 17 Arabs in civil unrest on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.
1991 - Haiti's parliament, watched by leaders of a military coup, formally installed the senior judge of the Supreme Court, Joseph Nerette, as the country's provisional president.

1993 - The U.N. General Assembly lifted almost all its remaining economic sanctions against South Africa, begun in the 1960s and built up in subsequent years because of Pretoria's policy of racial apartheid.
